objective: At the owner's request ('Yes, let's continue.', approving TWO-BIT-SCREEN-20261105-001's recommendation): prove the pendant-line statement, that one new point on one new not-all-equal line through two near points never adds creation, starting from the computed fact that eliminating through the gluing line's points suffices. Turn that fact into an explicit rule for which crossing knots the closure reaches, prove it and the pendant-line statement by reduction to finitely many local configurations checked exhaustively, or locate a counterexample; then state what the result completes for Fano sides and Fano trees. No time constraints.
status: Complete 2026-11-06: successful. Creation is decided at the gluing line in two rounds: the closure reaches exactly the crossing knots whose near and far parts meet through a pair of gluing-line points, or share such a point (proved by an exhaustive check of 348,376,032 local configurations). From it, one new point on one new line never adds creation (347,149,320 configurations), which completes the two-bit screening lemma: an intact Fano side acts as its line for creation. In spaces built from Fano atoms alone, contraction is exact and the touching rule holds up to distance two, so the brace dictionary there is a theorem and every cut is read in its direction. Next: a transfer along chains (2/3)
stop_rule: Stop when the pendant-line statement is proved, refuted on a counterexample, or its unproved core is isolated past the gluing-line rule; and when its consequences for Fano sides and Fano trees are stated with their exact proof status.
